clue.text: Mere visitors make it crowded at holiday time

definitions.text: Mere visitors make it crowded at holiday time

parts.words: Mere visitors make it crowded at holiday time
parts.note: a mere is a lake, so the visitors are tourists who throng a lakeland region of north-west England in the holiday season

explanation.surface: A remark about some pond or holiday spot being packed with sightseers during the summer break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like 'only', but it is the noun for a lake, which points to the famous English lakeland national park in Cumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cumbrian national park is full of lakes and is overrun by tourists in the summer holidays.

clue.text: Refuse to eat sticky stuff, green food

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the dregs swallow the sticky stuff

parts.note: lees are the sediment or dregs, refuse left in a wine vessel
gum is a sticky substance

explanation.surface: A child refuses to eat a gummy plate of greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, as in declining to eat, but it is the noun for rubbish, here the dregs.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas and beans are pod vegetables, the green food of the pulse family.

clue.text: Criticise holy place in Ireland

definitions.meaning: ... in County Mayo is a Marian shrine and place of pilgrimage

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a sacred Irish pilgrimage site.
explanation.walkthrough: The village of Knock, County Mayo, is famed for a reported apparition of the Virgin Mary in 1879.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something down is to criticise it; the Mayo village is a Catholic pilgrimage shrine.

clue.text: A fuss after mother's given ornament

indicators.note: after places the article and the fuss behind the word for mother

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
to make a scene is to make a fuss

explanation.surface: A child throws a tantrum after being handed one of mum's trinkets.
explanation.definitionFit: To damascene is to decorate metal with inlaid gold or silver patterns, so it means to ornament.

clue.text: Culmination of action about the big year coming up

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the legal action goes round the year

parts.note: a suit is a legal action
MM is 2000 in Roman numerals, the millennium year then approaching

explanation.surface: A climax of activity is expected around the approaching millennium.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in 1999, so the 'big year coming up' was 2000, MM in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the highest point, the peak or culmination of something.

clue.text: Rex — Joy's brother, perhaps

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, king
elation is joy; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A family introduction: Rex is Joy's brother.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex and Joy look like people's names, but one is the Latin for king and the other a feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother is one example of a family member or kinsman.

clue.text: Child's beginning to get isolated? Dolly may be the answer

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its first letter, here of the word for child

parts.note: lone means alone or isolated

explanation.surface: A child left on its own may be comforted by its doll.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly the sheep, born in 1996, was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, so she is a fair example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolly the sheep was a genetic copy of another animal, the most famous such duplicate.

clue.text: After a time, black pencil mark may well be

indicators.note: After places the word for black behind the word for a time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sable is the heraldic word for black

explanation.surface: Over time, a dark pencil mark is likely to be rubbed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil line can usually be rubbed out, so it is removable with a rubber.

clue.text: Runner on island

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An athlete is jogging on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link word, but in cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A legman is a reporter or errand-runner who gathers news or runs errands on foot.

clue.text: Good opportunity for a stable employee

parts.note: room, as in 'room for improvement', means scope or opportunity

explanation.surface: A promising opening for someone looking for work at a racing stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable hand who looks after horses is the employee in question, a sense distinct from a bridegroom.

clue.text: I had central role in Victoria's early development

definitions.text: I had central role in Victoria's early development

parts.words: I had central role in Victoria's early development
parts.note: read as the young Queen Victoria, the speaker is her first Prime Minister and mentor; read as the Australian state of Victoria, the speaker is its capital city, founded early in its history

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of being a key influence on a young queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Melbourne was Prime Minister at Victoria's accession in 1837 and guided her early reign; the city named after him is the capital of the Australian state of Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whig Prime Minister tutored the young queen, and the city of that name grew up as the centre of the Australian colony.

clue.text: Create relay of 'workers serving in emergency

parts.note: to make something is to create it
a shift is a group of workers who take turns with another group

explanation.surface: A manager arranges a rota of extra staff to cope with a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improvised and temporary is used as a stopgap when nothing better is available.

clue.text: Surrey town records great honour for citizen

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
the OM, Order of Merit, is a high British honour

explanation.surface: A local newspaper reports that a Surrey resident has received a great distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is one of Britain's most exclusive honours, limited to a small number of living members.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey town is famous for its racecourse, home of the Derby.

clue.text: Joining agency that's private? Not I

indicators.note: placed before the letter, 'Not' says that letter is to be left out of the word for a private

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dating or employment agency is private and denies being so.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Not I'; the OCR turned the I into an exclamation mark. 'private' wants to describe the agency, but it is a noun for the lowest-ranked soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Solder is the metal alloy that bonds two pieces of metal, so it is the means of joining.

clue.text: Clever class left going over the same thing again? It's not on

indicators.note: saying the next word is not there means its letters are removed from the repetition

parts.words: going over the same thing again
parts.note: iteration is repetition, doing something over again

explanation.surface: Bright people find repetition tedious and object to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's not on' looks like an objection; it tells you to drop ON from ITERATION.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read, educated people, an intellectual elite.

clue.text: Record vehicle in wooden hut

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
a cab is a taxi, a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diary entry noting that someone sat in a car parked by a timber shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontier dwelling built from tree trunks is a simple timber hut.

clue.text: What's disturbed me -loud car — made a big din

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone woken by a noisy car complains that it made a terrible racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges ME, LOUD and CAR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamour is to make a loud, insistent noise, to raise a din.

clue.text: A monkey holding a little stone in the foot

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the phrase for a monkey goes round the article

parts.note: a monkey is an ape, so 'A monkey' is an ape, written with the article
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A monkey is limping with a small pebble stuck in its foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' looks like part of the monkey; it is a metrical foot in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An anapaest is a metrical foot of two short syllables followed by a long one.

clue.text: Very cold polar regions for birds

parts.note: bitter weather is very cold
N, north, is one polar region
S, south, is the other polar region

explanation.surface: Birds migrate away from freezing Arctic and Antarctic lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterns are wading birds of the heron family, known for their booming call.

clue.text: Schism involving bishop and king coming to a head

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
R stands for Rex, king
each means per head, as in 'a pound each'

explanation.surface: A church split in which a bishop and a king come to a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to a head' suggests a crisis, but it means 'per head', each.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a rift or split between parties, much like a schism.

clue.text: Only just see behind obstacle

parts.note: a bar is a barrier or obstacle
Ely is a cathedral city and so a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A spectator can barely make out what is happening from behind a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places the see after the obstacle. A see is the seat of a bishop, and Ely in Cambridgeshire is one of the crossword's favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by the narrowest margin is done scarcely, with almost nothing to spare.

clue.text: One may be assumed by Muslim woman to have a narrow outlook

definitions.text: One may be assumed by Muslim woman to have a narrow outlook

parts.words: One may be assumed by Muslim woman to have a narrow outlook
parts.note: it reads as narrow-mindedness assumed of a woman, but 'assumed' means put on: a face veil leaves only a slit to see through

explanation.surface: A complaint that a Muslim woman might be presumed to be narrow-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumed' means donned, and 'narrow outlook' is literal: the veil covers the face below the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is a veil worn by some Muslim women in public, covering the lower face.

clue.text: Jazz pianist playing after note on horn

indicators.note: after puts the word for playing behind the hunting call

parts.note: a mort is the note sounded on a hunting horn at the death of the deer
on means taking place, as a show that is on

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist plays after a horn player sounds a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Jelly Roll Morton was an early New Orleans jazz pianist and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly Roll Morton was a pioneering New Orleans jazz pianist of the 1920s.

clue.text: English education, basically, admitting old mistake

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so the letter for old goes inside the other letters

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of education

explanation.surface: A complaint that basic English teaching has let in an outdated blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The O goes between the second and third R of E plus RRR.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a slip or blunder, the same thing as a mistake.

clue.text: Row brings fury right up to the surface

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing a letter up to the surface moves it to the top

parts.note: anger is fury

explanation.surface: An argument brings someone's rage bubbling to the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line, as in a range of hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a line or series of things, like a row of mountains.

clue.text: Jersey, etc, for leader to carry in trunk

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: a container carries what it holds, so the leader's letters hold the islands' letters

parts.note: a boss is a leader
CI is the Channel Islands, of which Jersey is one

explanation.surface: Instructions for a chief to pack a sweater and other items into a travel chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' and 'trunk' suggest clothes and luggage, but Jersey is the Channel Island and the trunk is an elephant's.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's long flexible nose is called its trunk.

clue.text: Animal fur one has on

indicators.note: in a down entry, the letter for one has the coat on top of it

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An animal wears its fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a South American mammal of the raccoon family.

clue.text: Can't get small number to work out in mathematical ratio

indicators.note: letters set to work out a solution are rearranged into the right order

parts.note: NO is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A student complains about being unable to calculate a figure in a trigonometry problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work out' rearranges CANT, GET and NO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry the cotangent of an angle is the ratio of the adjacent side to the opposite side.

clue.text: It has a sovereign, not invariably male

definitions.text: It has a sovereign, not invariably male

parts.note: R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

indicators.note: something not invariable has changed, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a kingdom has a monarch, who need not always be a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not invariably' rearranges MALE to EALM, after R. The whole clue also defines: a kingdom has a monarch who may be king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is ruled by a monarch, who may be a king or a queen.

clue.text: Get together for a beer, say? That could be a source of great pleasure

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt, so meeting sounds like the food word

parts.note: to meet up and have a drink together

explanation.surface: Someone suggests going out for a pint, which would be a real treat.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for something one relishes is spelt with the food word, not the word for coming together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is 'meat and drink to you' is what you enjoy or thrive on most.
